applies_to: KEBA KeContact E10 energy meter (companion meter for KeContact wallboxes and PV home systems), register list v1.00 (03.2024).
summary: The KeContact E10 is KEBA's three-phase smart energy meter for home energy management with its wallboxes. It answers Modbus with holding registers only: instantaneous power, current, voltage, power factor and frequency, 64-bit energy counters per phase, a fast block for current/voltage/power, a plug-and-play identity block, a SunSpec common + meter (203) model, and a few configuration, identify and restart registers.

addressing.note: The list gives start addresses, not register numbers: the first block starts at address 0 and the SunSpec block at 40000. The sheet itself warns that SunSpec register 40001 is read at address 40000.

source.title: KeContact E10 - Modbus Register List
source.pages: XLSX sheet 'E10 Modbus Register List' (all blocks) and sheet 'Description' (multi-register order, scaling examples)

notes: Multi-register values are most significant word first: the description sheet says the lower address holds the most significant bits and gives a uint32 example (0x0023 then 0x0044). 64-bit energy counters follow the same rule.
Engineering values: power in 0.1 W/var/VA steps, current and voltage in 0.001 A/V, power factor in 0.001, frequency in 0.001 Hz, energy in 0.1 Wh/varh/VAh.
SunSpec values use scale-factor registers that KEBA says can change at run time; always read the scale factor with the value.
All data is read with function 03 (read holding registers); configuration registers accept 06 and 16.
Static IP and subnet mask take one octet per register (4 registers each); network changes take effect after a restart (61615).

In the SunSpec block the list shows 0x8000 (SunSpec 'not implemented') for total current 40072 and the average voltages 40077/40081, 0x8000 for the reactive-energy scale factor 40174, and 0 for the var-hour quadrant counters; use the per-phase values and the native energy counters instead.
Reading an address that is not in the list returns exception 02. Reserved gaps are not listed.
Bus settings other than the baud-rate code (register 258) are not given in the list, so defaults are left empty.

integration.summary: Read the 64-bit energy counters at 512 (import) and 516 (export) and the per-phase power/current/voltage block 0-147, or use the SunSpec meter model at 40070 if your system speaks SunSpec. All values are big-endian, high word first.
integration.enable: Modbus RTU baud rate is set in register 258 (0 = 9600 ... 5 = 115200). IP address, subnet mask and DHCP are in registers 259-267 and take effect after a restart.
quirks: Read all registers of a multi-register value in one request.
Writing 1 to register 268 locks all configuration and the restart register; plan the configuration first.
setup: Registers 61613/61614 make the meter blink for identification on site.
gotchas: Power values are split into + (import) and - (export) registers, both unsigned, rather than one signed value.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
